                                 SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
                                   PUCT DOCKET NO. 59475

  APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC                       §     BEFORE THE STATE OFFICE
  DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA                       §
  TRANSMISSION            SERVICE                     §
  CORPORATION     TO AMEND ITS                        §                     ON
  CERTIFICATE OF CONVENIENCE AND                      §
  NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY                       §
  EAST   SWITCH    TO  BIG   HILL                     §
  SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION                      §    ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS
  LINE PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET,                       §
  CONCHO,   CORYELL,   LAMPASAS,                      §
  LLANO,    MASON,    MCCULLOCH,                      §
  MENARD, MILAM, MILLS, SAN SABA,                     §
  SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN, AND                          §
  WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                                 §

 BAR H BAR RANCH AND NATURE PRESERVE’S REPLIES TO EXCEPTIONS AND
             CORRECTION TO THE PROPOSAL FOR DECISION



         COMES NOW Scimitar Partners LP and Bar H Bar Land & Cattle Co. (collectively, “Bar

H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve” or “ranch”) and files this reply to exceptions and corrections

to the State Office of Administrative Hearings’ (“SOAH”) Proposal for Decision (“PFD”) related

to Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (“Oncor”) and LCRA Transmission Services

Corporation’s (“LCRA”) (collectively, the “Joint Applicants”) proposed 765-kilovolt (“kV”)

transmission line from the Bell Count East Switch to the Big Hill Substation. The deadline to file

replies to corrections and exceptions to the PFD is September 9, 2026, therefore this pleading is

timely filed.

         As Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve has provided throughout this proceeding,

selection of any route that utilizes links H1 and G52 will have a devastating effect on the ranch.

However, Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve wants to note that route 894 is not just bad for

one ranch, it is bad for central Texas all together. Save the Lampasas, a group of more than 50


                                                1
HB: 4910-0871-7518.1
 intervenors with over 550 interested members, aptly provided the devastating effects of route 894.

Save the Lampasas stated that route 894 “bisect[s] an inordinate number of properties through

previously undisturbed sensitive portions of the Study Area, crosses the Colorado River at a

previously undisturbed portion of the river to the detriment of Texas Parks and Wildlife

Department (TPWD) Colorado Bend State Park and Post Oak Ridge State Park, unnecessarily

negatively impacts the Lampasas River Valley, and implicates unaddressed engineering

constraints, among other concerns.” 1                The Soluna Ranch Intervenors further discussed the

devastating impacts of route 894 bisecting their ranch and causing devastating viewshed impacts

to the Colorado River. 2 Cherokee Creek Aligned Intervenors, a group of multiple central Texas

landowners, provided further evidence of how significantly route 894 affects multiple

environmental factors including the Colorado River, San Saba River, Edwards Aquifer, and

multiple endangered species in the area. 3 This is just a snapshot of the greater concern with route

894 that is shared by countless landowners in central Texas. Route 894 not only will have

devastating effects on ranches like Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve’s, but it also will be

significantly more environmentally harmful to central Texas. If the Commission rejects the PFD

and selects a route, we urge the Commission to not select route 894 as it is bad for landowners and

bad for Texas.

       I.       REPLIES TO EXCEPTIONS AND CORRECTIONS

            Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve appreciates the work of the SOAH Administrative

Law Judges (“ALJ”) in preparing the PFD and strongly agrees with the PFD’s recommendation to



1
    Initial Brief of Save the Lampasas at 3 (Jun. 19, 2026).
2
    Initial Brief of the Solana Intervenors at 3 and 6 (Jun. 19, 2026).
3
    Cherokee Creek Aligned Intervenors Initial Post-Hearing Brief at 5-6 (Jun. 19, 2026).


                                                               2
HB: 4910-0871-7518.1
 deny the application for failure of the Joint Applicants to provide adequate notice and that Joint

Applicants failed to establish that that the Certificate of Convenience and Necessity (“CCN”)

amendment was necessary for the service, accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public. 4

However, Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve disagrees with the PFD’s alternative

recommendation regarding selection of route 894 as the route that should be selected in this

proceeding, should the Public Utility Commission of Texas (“Commission” or “PUCT”) disagree

with the PFD’s recommendation to deny the application. 5 Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve’s

replies to exceptions in this pleading will focus on responding to Joint Applicants, Commission

Staff, and parties who support reasonable alternative routes to routes 894 and 487.

                  A. Reply to Joint Applicants

            Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve notes that it did not litigate the issue of due process

which is discussed in the PFD’s reasoning for denying the application. However, Bar H Bar Ranch

and Nature Preserve does wish to provide replies in support of the PFD on these issues. For many

landowners it feels like the proceeding itself is simply a pretense to a pre-determined outcome in

which they have no say. Yet incorrectly Joint Applicants argue that the PFD’s allegations that due

process was violated do not “withstand scrutiny and undermine longstanding Commission

practice.” 6 Joint Applicants here ask the Commission to ignore due process concerns because they

desperately want to ram through this application despite the numerous concerns with due process

and fairness. Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve believes the PFD did not touch on this issue

enough. The PFD states that the intervention deadline was on April 27, 2026, and the hearing was



4
    Proposal for Decision with Memorandum at 162 (Aug. 20, 2026) (“PFD”).
5
    Id. at 162.
6
    Applicants’ Exceptions to the Proposal for Decision at 5 (Sept. 2, 2026).


                                                            3
HB: 4910-0871-7518.1
 held on the second week of June 2026. 7 That does tell the true story of how compressed the timeline

was for this proceeding. From the intervention deadline to the hearing parties had to file testimony,

prepare exhibits, conduct discovery, and be ready for hearing all in what amounts to 45 days. There

was not realistically enough time to get more than one or two discovery requests to the Joint

Applicants in that time and not nearly enough time to marshal a reasonable defense. All in all,

landowners were given what amounts to a month and a half to prepare a defense of their ranches,

their homes, and their livelihoods. While on the other hand the Joint Applicants had over a year to

prepare their application and be ready to support it throughout the proceeding. Further, the PFD

under sells the cross-examination time limits imposed on the hearing. In many cases, parties had

less than three minutes to cross-examine the Joint Applicants’ professional witnesses in this

proceeding. To put that in perspective, if a witness wished to filibuster during their response, which

many of them did, then a party was able to ask maybe two or three questions of that witness before

their time ran out. Joint Applicants argue to the Commission that two or three minutes of cross-

examination is more than enough due process to take their land and destroy the value of their

properties. We disagree with the Joint Applicants, the Commission should not allow what

amounted to an unreasonable limitation of exercise of landowners’ statutory rights to be justified

so that Joint Applicants can build a transmission line the PFD has recommended is not needed.

Instead, the Commission should reject the application and adopt the PFD’s recommendations.

           Further, the PFD highlights another important due process concern, that is the ability of

parties to reasonably review and respond to testimony. The PFD points out that Commission

Staff’s witness John Poole had sorted testimony in alphabetical order and had only reviewed




7
    Proposal for Decision at 49-50 (Aug. 20, 2026).


                                                      4
HB: 4910-0871-7518.1
 through “F” as of the date of his testimony and through “O” by the date of his deposition. 8 We

appreciate Mr. Poole’s forthrightness and that shows that even Commission Staff’s witness, whose

job is to review and respond to pleadings in this proceeding, could not timely process the amount

of information filed in this docket. This further shows that the overwhelming amount of Joint

Applicant and Intervenor testimony was almost impossible for any party to get through. However,

for most landowners who have regular 9-5 jobs, it would be next to impossible to read and

comprehend the vast amount of testimony filed with such a short time to review. We urge the

Commission to reject this notion and not allow landowners to have their properties taken when

they were not afforded reasonable due process.

               B. Reply to Commission Staff

           We note that Commission Staff disagrees with the selection of route 894 and argues instead

for the selection of route 487. 9 While we think other routes better address the requirements in

PURA, Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve strongly prefers route 487 proposed by Commission

Staff to route 894 proposed by Joint Applicants. As has been outlined extensively in filings made

by Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve, selection of any route that utilizes link H1, which bisects

the ranch, will have devastating effects on the ranch and its continued operations. 10 Unlike route

894, route 487 only utilizes link G52 which crosses the northern portion of the ranch. Though this

will have negative impacts on the ranch, those impacts will be far less harmful to ranch operations

than route 894 which utilizes both links H1 and G52. To the extent the Commission does not deny

the application as recommended by the PFD, Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve urges the


8
    Proposal for Decision at 51 (Aug. 20, 2026).
9
    Commission Staff’s Exceptions to the Proposal for Decision at 14 (Sept. 2, 2026).
10
   See generally, Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve Initial Brief (Jun. 19, 2026); Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature
Preserve Reply Brief (Jun. 26, 2026).


                                                           5
HB: 4910-0871-7518.1
 Commission to select a route that does not utilize link H1, including potentially selecting

Commission Staff’s recommended route 487.

                C. Reply to Other Party Recommendations

           Many other parties have provided support for various alternative routes to Joint Applicant’s

recommended route, route 894, and Commission Staff’s recommended route, route 487. Save the

Lampasas 11, G-9 and G-13 Landowners 12, and Carpenter Land and Cattle Co. 13 all recommended

route 296 as the route that best meets the requirements in PURA. Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature

Preserve would support selection of route 296, to the extent the Commission rejects the ultimate

recommendation in the PFD and agrees with the reasoning provided by the parties for its selection.

Further, route 296 does not suffer from the issues with selection of a route that utilizes links H1

and G52. Next, Solana Intervenors 14 and Staten Creek Ranch 15 recommend selection of route 392

as a reasonable alternative to route 894 or route 487. Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve would

also support selection of route 392, to the extent the Commission rejects the ultimate

recommendation in the PFD and agrees with the reasoning provided by the parties for its selection.

Route 392 also does not suffer from the issues with selection of a route that utilizes links H1 and

G52. Lastly, Cherokee Creek Aligned Intervenors 16 recommend selection of Route CCG as a

reasonable alternative to routes 894 and 487. Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve would also




11
  Save the Lampasas Exceptions to the Alternative Recommendation In the Proposal for Decision at 28 (Sept. 2,
2026).
12
     G-9 and G-13 Landowners’ Exceptions to the Proposal for Decision at 15-16 (Sept. 2, 2026).
13
   Carpenter Land and Cattle Co.’s Limited Exceptions to the Alternative Recommendation in the Proposal for
Decision at 17 (Sept. 2, 2026).
14
     Solana Intervenors’ Exceptions to the Proposal for Decision at 30-31 (Sept. 2, 2026).
15
     Staten Creek Ranch’s Exceptions to the Proposal for Decision at 40 (Sept. 2, 2026).
16
     Exceptions to the Proposal for Decision by Cherokee Creek Aligned Intervenors at 15-16 (Sept. 2, 2026).


                                                            6
HB: 4910-0871-7518.1
 support selection of Route CCG. All of these routes provide a reasonable alternative to routes 894

and 487 and none of these recommended routes utilize links H1 or G52. Bar H Bar Ranch and

Nature Preserve sees the merit in selection of any of these routes, where the Commission to reject

the PFD, and would urge the Commission to select one of these routes over route 894 or 487.

    II.       CONCLUSION

          As outlined above, Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve agrees with the PFD’s

recommendation to reject the application but disagrees with much of the reasoning in the PFD

regarding its alternative recommendation to select route 894 as the route that best meets the PURA

factors. Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve urges the Commission to adopt the PFD’s ultimate

recommendation to reject the application, but to the extent the Commission approves the

application we urge the Commission to reject the PFD and select a route other than route 894 or

any route that utilizes links H1 and G52.




                                                7
HB: 4910-0871-7518.1
 Dated: September 9, 2026


                              Respectfully submitted,
